The first PT_PROF sweep printed nothing because the scratch build's shaders failed to compile at startup, so no frame ever ran and no benchmark line was produced. When I added the profiling bits I wrote the PT_PROF tests in pt_trace.metal against a bare identifier `params`, but inside pt_intersect_scene the only thing in scope is the PtScene struct — the parameters are reached through `scene.params->pad`. MTLDevice newLibraryWithSource therefore returned a compile error ("undeclared ... params"), the host bailed out of the dispatch path, and every PT_PROF=... invocation exited without printing render_ms/gpu_ms. Once I changed those references to scene.params->pad the sweep worked and produced the cost shares I recorded: full 45.35ms, no shadow walk 44.05ms (~1.3ms), no NEE 43.17ms (~2.2ms), no mesh closest-hit 4.77ms — i.e. the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame (that drove all of round 5's later experiments).

How I know: my own history for this round — messages 43-50 added the four biased PT_PROF bits to the _prof copy, 54-56 record the shader compile error in pt_intersect_scene and the fix to use scene.params->pad, and 58 records the first successful run of the sweep with the numbers above. A related trap I hit later in the same round (messages 68-76) was different in cause but identical in symptom: a cp -R nesting bug left ab_r4/include/include, so that base binary also printed nothing because its shaders disagreed with the round-4 headers — which is why I now always check that a candidate/base prints a benchmark line before trusting an A/B.

The scratch profiling build in _prof/ was silently failing at runtime shader compilation, so it never got to the benchmark loop and printed no timing line at all.

What happened: to carry the PT_PROF bitmask I added a `pad` field to PtParams and wrote the biased skip bits into the traversal helpers in pt_trace.metal. Those helpers take only the PtScene, not the params, so my first edit referenced a bare `params` inside pt_intersect_scene, which does not exist. I fixed it by reading the mask through scene.params->pad and the sweep then produced the cost shares (full 45.35ms, no-shadow 44.05, no-NEE 43.17, no-mesh 4.77 → the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame).

How I know: my working-memory entry "round5-cost-shares" records the scratch build in _prof/ with params.pad carrying the PT_PROF mask and those measured shares (evidence #31-58), and the archived index for messages 30-120 lists the fix at #54-56 ("shader compile error 'undeclared params' in pt_intersect_scene -> use scene.params->pad") immediately before the successful sweep at #58. answer:
The profiling build was failing at startup, not running silently — and my sweep command hid the reason.

What was wrong: the PT_PROF edit I had made in the scratch shader _prof/shaders/pt_trace.metal tested the profiling bitmask as a bare `params.pad` inside pt_intersect_scene, but that function has no local `params` (it only sees the scene struct, so the correct reference is `scene.params->pad`). Because this program compiles its Metal sources at runtime with newLibraryWithSource, the C++ build succeeded and produced _prof/pathtracer, but every launch aborted during Metal init with:

  metal init error: shader compile failed: program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'
      if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(scene, ray, mesh_t, mesh_normal)) {

So no frame was ever rendered and no 'render_ms_best=...' line was ever printed. My sweep loop also piped stderr to /dev/null and kept only `tail -1` of stdout, which is why the output was six bare 'PT_PROF=n' lines with nothing after them.

How I know it: the sweep is archived at message #52 (all six lines empty); #53 re-ran the binary directly with stderr shown and #54 printed the exact compile error above; #55 fixed the reference to `scene.params->pad` (no rebuild needed, since shaders compile at runtime); #58 re-ran the same sweep and produced the cost shares I still use — gpu_ms_best full 45.352, no-shadow 44.051, no-NEE 43.171, no-mesh 4.773 (⇒ the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame), glass always-reflect 35.764.

The general lesson I recorded from this round's sibling bug (the ab_r4 base binary printing nothing because a `cp -R` nesting error left include/include and the shaders failed to compile): a silent run here almost always means a runtime shader-compile failure, so always check stderr once before trusting an empty result.
